subject: sentences
title: Longer stories
about: Three-sentence stories, and a few true animal and weather facts, each followed by a who, what, where, why or when question whose answer is right there in the text. NC RL.1.1 and RI.1.1 ask first graders to answer questions about key details in stories and in information texts.
tip: If he picks wrong, do not give the answer: read the story again together and have him stop you at the sentence that tells it.

cards.q: Mia had a loose tooth. She wiggled it all day. At last it fell out! What fell out?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The first sentence names it: a loose tooth.

cards.q: Ben made a sand castle. Then a big wave came. Splash! The castle was gone. What made the castle go away?
cards.note: The wave came, then the castle was gone. The wave is what did it.

cards.q: Zoe got a letter in the mail. It was from her aunt. It had a photo of a horse! Who sent the letter?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. From her aunt tells us who sent it.

cards.q: Max went to the zoo with Dad. They saw a tall giraffe eat leaves. Who went with Max?
cards.note: Who asks about a person. With Dad tells us.

cards.q: It rained all morning. Liv could not go out. So she read a book by the window. Why did Liv stay in?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: it rained.

cards.q: Jon got a new puppy named Pepper. Pepper likes to chew socks. What does Pepper chew?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The story says socks.

cards.q: A frog can breathe through its skin. So a frog must keep its skin wet. What must a frog keep wet?
cards.note: This one is a fact. Frogs really do breathe through their skin, so it has to stay wet.

cards.q: Owls hunt at night. Their big eyes help them see in the dark. When do owls hunt?
cards.note: This is a fact. When asks about a time: at night.

cards.q: Snow is made of tiny bits of ice. It falls when the air is very cold. When does snow fall?
cards.note: This is a fact. The second sentence tells when snow falls.

cards.q: A camel lives in the hot, dry desert. It can go many days with no water. Where does a camel live?
cards.note: This is a fact. Where asks about a place: the desert.

cards.q: A rainbow comes when the sun shines on rain. It has seven colors. How many colors does a rainbow have?
cards.note: This is a fact. How many asks for a number: seven.

cards.q: Sam made soup with Grandma. They cut up carrots and peas. It smelled so good! What did Sam make?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The first sentence says soup.

cards.q: Ben's bike had a flat tire. He walked it to the shop. Now it rolls again! Why did Ben walk his bike?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. The first sentence gives it: a flat tire.

cards.q: Mia and Max made a blanket fort. They read books inside it with a flashlight. Where did they read?
cards.note: Where asks about a place: inside the fort.

cards.q: Our class has a pet turtle named Tank. Tank eats lettuce and naps on a rock. What does Tank eat?
cards.note: What asks about a thing. The second sentence says lettuce.

cards.q: Jon could not reach the top shelf. He stood on a stool. Then he got the game! Why did Jon use a stool?
cards.note: Why asks for a reason. He could not reach, so he stood on a stool.
